developments: Bitcoin rallied nearly $3,000 from its session low and traded near $60,260 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, up about $1,700 since the afternoon edition.
US stocks recovered most of the morning's sell-off: the Dow turned positive and the Nasdaq was down under 1% late in the session, Yahoo Finance reported, against about 4% at the open.
ZEC bounced about 10% from the afternoon to near $761, above where it started the day.
briefing.changed: Much calmer than the afternoon. The PCE and tariff shock faded as stocks clawed back, and bitcoin went from breaking $58,500 to retaking $60,000. The month is still on track to be bitcoin's worst since June 2022, so one rebound does not change the wider picture.
briefing.question: Is this rebound the start of a recovery, or a relief bounce in thin holiday trade before another test of $58,500?
briefing.watch: Friday's monthly BTC options expiry at 08:00 UK, with US markets shut on Thursday. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin retakes $60,000 as Wall Street claws back early losses
lead.standfirst: A late recovery in US shares lifted bitcoin nearly $3,000 from its morning low, though analysts warned that the month remains its worst in over four years.
body: Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000 on Wednesday afternoon in New York, turning positive for the day after rallying nearly $3,000 from its session low, CoinDesk reported. Kraken showed it near $60,260 at 21:30 UK, against a low of about $57,210.

The move tracked a recovery in US stocks. The Nasdaq, down about 4% at the open after hotter-than-expected core PCE inflation and new US tariff proposals, was down less than 1% late in the session, while the Dow turned positive, Yahoo Finance reported. The ten-year Treasury yield fell to 4.82% as investors bought bonds.
CoinDesk noted that investor Michael Burry said he had covered his technology shorts, which traders read as a sign of how stretched the selling had become.
Zcash rebounded more sharply, with ZEC near $761 on Kraken, up about 10% since the afternoon.

The wider picture stayed weak. Bitcoin was down about 24% in November, its worst month since June 2022, CoinDesk reported. Galaxy withdrew its call that the bear market had ended and said a daily close below $58,525 would point to lower lows.
US markets close on Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen for a half day on Friday, when monthly bitcoin options expire.

headline: Bitcoin rallied back above $60,000 as US stocks recovered most of their early losses, and ZEC bounced about 10%. November is still on course to be bitcoin's worst month since 2022.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, evening edition. After a rough start, US stocks clawed back most of the day's losses, and bitcoin followed, climbing nearly three thousand dollars from its low to around sixty thousand, two hundred. Zcash bounced about ten per cent to around seven hundred and sixty dollars. Galaxy has withdrawn its call that the bear market was over, and November is still bitcoin's worst month since twenty twenty-two. A House bill to make the bitcoin reserve law is now ready for a floor vote. US markets are shut tomorrow for Thanksgiving. Monthly bitcoin options expire on Friday at eight in the morning. The next red event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin rallies nearly $3,000 from its low to retake $60,000
stories.why: CoinDesk reported bitcoin back above $60,000 and positive for the day by 19:24 UK; Kraken showed about $60,260 at 21:30 UK, against a session low near $57,210. This afternoon it had only just recovered to $58,500, so the day now looks like a failed breakdown rather than a new leg lower.

note.read: Buyers stepped in once stocks steadied, and the close back above Galaxy's $58,525 line avoids the bearish signal it had flagged.
note.alt: Thin pre-holiday trading and short covering can produce sharp bounces that fade; bitcoin is still on course for an eighth straight weekly loss, CoinDesk said.
note.change: A drop back below $58,500 on a daily close would revive the breakdown case; holding above $60,000 through Friday's expiry would support the recovery case.

stories.title: US stocks claw back most of the PCE and tariff sell-off
stories.why: About 50 minutes before the close, the Dow was up about 0.4%, the S&P 500 down 0.4% and the Nasdaq down 0.9%, Yahoo Finance reported, after a 4% Nasdaq drop at the open. The ten-year yield fell to 4.82%. Markets still price about a 98% chance of a December Fed rise.
stories.caveat: Figures are late intraday levels, not confirmed closing prices.

note.read: The quick recovery suggests the morning drop was partly positioning, which eased pressure on crypto.
note.alt: Tech stayed weak and Nvidia was still down about 5%, so the AI-spending worry has not gone away.
note.change: Another heavy tech sell-off on Friday's half day would put bitcoin back under pressure.

stories.title: ZEC rebounds about 10% to near $761
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC near $761 at 21:30 UK, up from about $688 at the afternoon edition and above its day open near $739. It fell harder than bitcoin on the way down and bounced harder on the way up, with no Zcash-specific news found, which fits a high-beta move with the market.

stories.title: Galaxy withdraws its 'bear market is over' call
stories.why: Galaxy's Alex Thorn withdrew October's view that the bear market ended in June, CoinDesk reported, and said a daily close below $58,525 would signal lower lows, with history pointing to about $48,500. 21Shares named about $53,000, near bitcoin's realised price, as the next support.

stories.title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill is now ready for a House floor vote
stories.why: H.R. 8957, which would write the US bitcoin reserve into law and bar sales for 20 years, was formally reported by the House Financial Services Committee on Tuesday and placed on the House calendar, Bitcoin Magazine reported. No vote is scheduled, and the Senate would also need to act.

stories.title: Attackers hijack mining hashrate over unencrypted pool connections
stories.why: Mining pool Braiins said attackers impersonated pools on the older Stratum V1 protocol to divert up to 1.9 EH/s from more than 1,000 sites, sending rewards to their own wallets, The Block reported. It affects miners, not bitcoin holders or the network's rules, and Braiins urged a move to encrypted Stratum V2.

explained.title: Realised price
body: Bitcoin's realised price is the average price at which every coin last moved on the blockchain. It is a rough guide to what the average holder paid.

When the market price falls towards it, as 21Shares suggested around $53,000, the typical holder is close to breaking even, which some analysts treat as a level where selling pressure tends to ease. It is a rule of thumb, not a floor.

investigating: Did Wednesday's ETF flows break the six-day outflow streak? Evidence: Farside or SoSoValue data on Thursday morning.
Will Friday's monthly options expiry pull bitcoin towards a particular price? Evidence: Deribit open interest and max-pain level before 08:00 UK on Friday.
